Package com.codedstream.otterstream.runtime.feature

Class SlidingWindowFeatureProvider

java.lang.Object
com.codedstream.otterstream.runtime.feature.SlidingWindowFeatureProvider
All Implemented Interfaces:
FeatureProvider
public class SlidingWindowFeatureProvider extends Object implements FeatureProvider
A FeatureProvider that computes its feature value in real time from a sliding window of recently-recorded values, rather than looking one up from external storage — the "real-time feature computation" piece of the Feature Store Integration roadmap item. Feed it from your Flink pipeline as events arrive (e.g. one record(java.lang.String, double) call per transaction amount), and it answers "what's the rolling AggregationFunction for this entity over the last N minutes" on every fetch() — genuinely computed on the fly, not a cached lookup of a value someone else computed elsewhere.

Uses the same sliding-window-with-pruning technique as otter-control-plane-server's TopologyService on the TypeScript side: samples are pruned as a side effect of new writes for the same entity (bounding that entity's own memory), plus an explicit evictEntitiesIdleSince(long) for the caller to invoke periodically to bound total memory across all entities.

Usage


 SlidingWindowFeatureProvider avgTxnAmount = new SlidingWindowFeatureProvider(
         "avg-transaction-amount-5m", Duration.ofMinutes(5), AggregationFunction.AVG);

 // In your Flink pipeline, as each transaction arrives:
 avgTxnAmount.record(entityId, transaction.getAmount());

 // Feed the running average into the next inference call as a feature:
 Map<String, Object> features = avgTxnAmount.fetch(entityId, List.of());
 double runningAvg = (double) features.get("avg-transaction-amount-5m");

Cardinality caveat, stated plainly: memory is bounded per entity (old samples are pruned) but is not automatically bounded across the total number of distinct entity ids ever seen — a workload with unbounded/high-cardinality entity ids (e.g. one-off session ids rather than stable user/account ids) will grow this provider's memory unboundedly unless you call evictEntitiesIdleSince(long) periodically. This is the same caller-driven-pruning trade-off TopologyService makes on the Control Plane side, not an oversight.

  • Method Details

    • record

      public void record(String entityId, double value)
      Records one new value for an entity — call this from your pipeline as events arrive. Prunes this entity's own samples older than the window as a side effect, bounding its memory regardless of how long the provider has been running.
      Parameters:
      entityId - the entity this value belongs to
      value - the value to record

    • fetch

      public Map<String,Object> fetch(String entityId, List<String> featureNames)
      Returns the current aggregate for entityId over the trailing window. Ignores featureNames — this provider computes exactly one feature (itself), named after getProviderId(); a caller asking for a specific list of feature names from a generic FeatureProvider-typed reference will still get this one value back under that name.
      Specified by:
      fetch in interface FeatureProvider
      Parameters:
      entityId - the entity to fetch features for (e.g. a user or account id)
      featureNames - the names of the features to retrieve
      Returns:
      a map of feature name to feature value

    • evictEntitiesIdleSince

      public int evictEntitiesIdleSince(long maxIdleMillis)
      Removes entities whose last record(java.lang.String, double) call was more than maxIdleMillis ago — call this periodically (e.g. on a scheduled tick in your application) to bound total memory when entity cardinality is high or unbounded. See the class Javadoc's cardinality caveat.
      Returns:
      how many entities were evicted
